page: Amazon Web Services m8gn.4xlarge is a general-purpose server powered by the AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processor. Operating on the Nitro hypervisor, this instance features 16 dedicated physical cores running at 2.8 GHz with a single thread per core. The memory configuration consists of 64.0 GB of RAM, providing a balanced 4.0 GB per core ratio. It does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, relying entirely on network-attached storage and offering a baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate strong memory performance, with the Passmark memory score placing in the top 10% tier. Large-block uncached memory read and write bandwidths reach 296.75 GB/sec and 138.43 GB/sec respectively, both ranking in the top 25%. CPU performance is robust, with Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores in the top 25%, alongside strong bzip3 decompression and database operations. However, the instance exhibits weaker performance in LLM inference tasks, with text generation on a small model and prompt processing on a medium model falling into the bottom 25% tier.

The ARM64 architecture and dedicated core allocation deliver high resource density and memory bandwidth efficiency relative to its hardware class. The lack of local storage requires external block storage provisioning, which is a key architectural tradeoff. Given its strong database operations benchmark and high network throughput, the m8gn.4xlarge is suited for database hosting, memory-intensive caching, web serving, and general-purpose enterprise workloads that benefit from high memory bandwidth and dedicated vCPU allocation.
